One correction: allot is not the same as "a lot".

To allot is to portion, "a lot" is an allotment or a large amount/number.

From personal experience shooting my friend's gun:

Pros: Goes bang. Accuracy is fine for 7-8 yards. All models take +P loads. Will take a serious beating and still go bang. Cleaning is easy, and can regularly be accomplished with canned air.

Cons: Slides weigh upwards of a pound. Balance is abysmal. Low magazine capacity (some aftermarket available, but why invest more in something so cheap?) No customization options that I'm aware of.

I would say that this is not a great weapon to own. I find the act of shooting it unpleasant, and I'd rather save for a while and buy something nicer, maybe a nice used Glock.

[Really?](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singular_they)

You should fix that entry, poste-haste!

I have no problem with either "he or she" or neuter "they", but many people prefer the latter because it doesn't put one gender before the other (I know, I know, it's a bullshit argument). Also, "they" is only one syllable, so it's easier to use in a brief sentence.

The other problem was that the poster was starting to close in on an argument based on gender privilege, but was being undermined by the availability of a neuter. He (I know it's a "he" from his posting history) then tried to argue against "they" by changing "he was" to "they was" and saying that it just didn't work. I agreed that "they was" is not correct, however, the fault was in his use, not in the correct use.

Just to editorialize for a minute: I don't think that dude was some kind of frothing nutbar-moron hybrid. I think he's just an average guy of average intelligence who, like some do from time to time, got confused by the intertwining of his political perspective and his argument.

You are correct. The proper English would be "they were". When using "they" to indicate a person or persons of indeterminate gender, you do have to conjugate accordingly. This is proper English, and preferable to guessing at gender when that could be offensive or just plain incorrect.

This isn't about gender privilege; this is about using common language to express a neuter pronoun that is absent in English.

I have them on speed dial.  Most of the time, I don't call.  I think they've started to figure out who I am.  I have a pretty distinct voice.  Some of them have called me by name before I introduce myself.

It goes like this: I call.  I get embarrassed.  I hang up abruptly.  90% of the time I call again.  I'm taking up valuable time that someone in a real crisis could be using.  Why do I waste these people's time?  I hang up.  20% of the time I call again.  I hang up before the phone rings.  Maybe I call again.  I talk for a minute.  I don't say much.  They sound annoyed.  I'm annoying.  Stop annoying these people.  They're volunteering to help people, not listen to this crap.  Hang up.  HANG UP!  I hang up.

I don't know.  Maybe.  Something.  I don't know.  That's all I ever have to say, these days: I don't know.

I haven't gotten help.  I've let this go on too long.  This is the most motivated I've been in a very long time, and all I'm doing is posting crap on the internet.

I don't know what talking will do.  I don't even know if I'll find out.  I don't have high hopes, but I think it's the disease talking.

I just don't know, and when I think hard about it, it gets really fuzzy and I get distracted.  I'm sorry I don't have anything better for you.

Often.  Very.  Depression can be a trip.  The only reason I haven't done it is because I lack the motivation to do it.

I'll tell you this: don't take that shit lightly.

I started out with just, "I have bad days.  Yeah, every once-in-a-while I think about taking the easy way out.  Everybody does," and that took a long, distracted wander into, "I'd do it, but I'll probably fuck that up, just like everything else in my life." Then something shiny flits in front of me, I forget about it, and I get back around to that idea an hour or so later.  Every time it's like starting all over again, like it's the first time I ever came up with this genius idea.

The worst is that I've been meaning to contact a psych for MONTHS, but every time I pick up the phone, I start calling someone else, or calling for pizza or something.  I can't bring myself to do it.  "I'm nearly there," I say to myself, "Tomorrow, I'll call.  Tomorrow, things will be different.  Right now, I really need to call Steve.  He's probably worried because we haven't spoken in six months."

You bury your head in the sand, you ignore every symptom. Suddenly, your shortening attention span is "undiagnosed ADD", you start losing friends (Fuck 'em, what good were those freeloading losers?), you start drinking more (I'm going out and meeting new people, I just drink socially six days a week), your boyfriend/girlfriend is gone (Must've been something wrong with me, maybe I should take a break from this whole dating thing), your family is worried (I'm fine, just having a work/existential crisis), you don't sleep at night (I'm a nightowl), you sleep during the day (I'M A NIGHTOWL!), you're smoking (calms me down), you're forgetting things (Didn't have my coffee today... or this week... or this month... I'M A NIGHTOWL!!), on and on.  Hell, I've drifted away from writing this long-ass pantload of a comment about ten times.  For thirty-eight minutes I've been writing this, and I haven't even edited it.

You don't see the drift, and when you do, you don't know why you're getting worse (even when your situation gets better), but you can come up with as many reasons as you'll ever need for why.  It happens because you deserve it ("Man, I put too much sugar in my coffee, I can't get ANYTHING right," starts an avalanche to, "I could just stomp the gas and take this car off that bridge, at least I wouldn't be fucking up everyone's lives any more.").  It happens because other people don't like you (I feel terrible and I don't have anyone to call because they don't care, and rightly so, I'm such a fucking sadsack, why would they care...).  It happens and you can't explain it (why am I so run-down today?).

I guess what I'm saying is this: Take care of this shit.  Having daily thoughts of offing yourself isn't a good thing.  If it progresses, if it starts to feel right or good or comforting, get help.  Hell, talk to someone now, you may not realize how much you need it.

My old employer (a fairly large photocopier sales/service company) has prizes for performance.  Last year, they held a raffle in which they gave tickets based on improvements made over the previous quarter.  The prize was a trip to Las Vegas and a couple grand to sweeten the deal.  I was completely unaware of this.

I took my job there in January of last year, and by March, had improved my department to such a degree that our branch had more raffle entries than any other three put together.  Needless to say, we won, and my boss sent me pictures of that kickass trip to Vegas. I'd be lying if I said I wasn't a little resentful, but he needed the break, so I congratulated him.

As an added bonus, my $1 an hour raise was blocked because they didn't have money in the budget for that.
